name: Gilead Sciences

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Gilead Sciences Logo.svg, non-free logo file)

description: Gilead makes antiviral and cancer medicines. HIV treatment and prevention is about 70 percent of revenue, led by Biktarvy, a once-daily pill that alone is about 49 percent of the company. Other lines are liver disease (hepatitis B and C, and the PBC drug Livdelzi), cell therapy and Trodelvy in cancer, and Veklury for COVID-19. Money comes from drug sales, mostly to three US wholesalers (Cardinal Health, Cencora, McKesson, about 90 percent of US gross product sales) and from royalties. In 2025 it launched Yeztugo, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection, and in 2026 bought Tubulis and Ouro Medicines.

businessLines.name: HIV
businessLines.how: Long-term daily-pill therapy for people living with HIV, repeat prescriptions for years, sold through wholesalers at list price less rebates; newer prevention products (Descovy, Yeztugo) are sold to people who are not infected. Volume and net price both move revenue.
businessLines.description: Treatment and prevention; one of Gilead's products lines within its single reported operating segment.

businessLines.name: Liver disease
businessLines.how: Hepatitis C is a short cure course (fading volume); hepatitis B and PBC are chronic prescriptions. Sold through wholesalers and, outside the US, through distributors.
businessLines.description: Hepatitis B, C and PBC (Livdelzi, Vemlidy, Epclusa-type sofosbuvir/velpatasvir).

businessLines.name: Veklury (COVID-19)
businessLines.how: Hospital-administered antiviral, bought by hospitals and governments in proportion to COVID-19 hospitalisations.

businessLines.name: Oncology
businessLines.how: One-time personalised cell therapy (priced per patient, high price, treatment centres) plus Trodelvy, an infused cancer drug bought per treatment cycle.

businessLines.name: Royalty, contract and other revenues
businessLines.how: Royalties and partner contract income (FY2024: $144M; 2025 jump not explained in the text read).

brands.name: Ouro Medicines (acquired June 2026, about $1.9B including up to $500M contingent)
